outcome: Pictorial blood loss assessment chart scores
cohort: The study included 81 patients with adenomyosis who had undergone ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and attempted to conceive, out of 182 consecutive patients who had undergone RFA.
finding: Ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) resulted in a 35.8% pregnancy rate (50% for those actively trying to conceive) and 66.7% live birth rate, while also significantly improving blood loss and pain scores in patients with adenomyosis desiring to maintain fertility and alleviate symptoms.
mod_finding: Among the 29 patients who achieved pregnancies, there were nine vaginal deliveries and 15 cesarean sections for the 24 live babies.
followup_time: Up to 72 months (6 years) for conception, and 1, 3, and 6 months for symptomatic relief.
